fix: stop app.quit() on electron-updater Performance timing errors

electron-updater calls performance.measure() during network-based
update checks. A bug in certain 6.x versions passes an object where
a string mark name is expected, producing a SyntaxError with message
'The mark [object Object] does not exist'. This was hitting
uncaughtException which immediately called app.quit() — causing users
to see a crash dialog on every launch when connected to the internet.

- Filter the Performance SyntaxError out of uncaughtException so the
  app continues running (update check failure is non-fatal)
- Add unhandledRejection handler so async update failures are logged
  instead of silently dropping or crashing
- Bump electron-updater 6.3.9 -> 6.8.9 which contains the upstream
  fix for the performance.measure argument type bug

Add mzd-core: config, firmware compat, planner, renderer, safety checks

Pure pipeline: TOML/JSON config + host assets -> validated plan -> bundle
files (run.sh, manifest.json, README.txt, payload/). Output is
deterministic. Mode defaults to check, which runs preflight on the CMU
and changes nothing. Integration tests run the generated run.sh against
the fake CMU tree with every POSIX shell on the host: check mode, firmware
mismatch, failed anchors, idempotent apply, and uninstall restoring every
non-permanent file. JSON Schemas in data/schema are kept in sync by a test.

Add mzd-transport: Transport trait, USB layout writer, serial session

UsbBundle writes the stick layout, dry-run by default, refuses to clobber
an existing bundle. SerialSession speaks to the CMU console over any
Read+Write with marker-framed commands, kernel-log filtering, credential
fallback and a printf-based upload; tested against a scripted mock CMU.
Opening a real UART (115200 8N1, explicit /dev/tty* path) needs the
opt-in 'serial' feature. PowerControl is an interface plus a mock only;
power and GPIO stay outside this crate.

Install community-tested tweaks on CMU firmware v74+

tweaks.sh refused v74 outright (compatibility group 0). Owners have been
running AIO on 74.00.324 by editing the generated script so v74 takes the
v70 code paths, and have reported which tweaks work. This makes that
official, but only for the tweaks on the tested list.

- compatibility_check puts 74.00.xxx and later in a new group 8. Group 8
  uses the v70 files like group 6, but never runs v70_integrity_check,
  which would copy v70 fallback files onto a v74 unit.
- Tested tweaks whose scripts gate on firmware now take the v70 path on
  group 8 without prompting: main menu loop, list loop, no more
  disclaimer, audio source order (install and uninstall), date to
  statusbar, and the systemApp.js patch that lists speedometer and
  videoplayer. The "only tested up to v70" prompts stay for group 7.
- Tweaks not tested on v74 (Castscreen, AIO Tweaks App, Android Auto)
  and unlisted ones that change system files (Enable WiFi, SSH_bringback,
  Remove Background Overlays, MZD Meter, CASDK installs) are wrapped at
  build time in `if install_allowed "NAME"`, which skips them on group 8
  with a message. Pause on Mute, USB Audio Mod and FLAC were already
  skipped by their own checks.
- Integration test checks the wrapping.

Write each tweak once when no blank album art is chosen

With "Change Blank Album Art Frame" selected and no image chosen, reading
no_artwork_icon.png fails and a fallback copies the default after 3s.
Node 24's fs streams emit 'close' after that 'error' (Node 12 in Electron
6 didn't), so the 'close' handler continued the build too. buildTweak ran
twice and tweaks.sh contained every tweak twice.

Skip the 'close' handlers when the stream errored. Integration test
compiles that case and checks the tweak appears once.
